item.title: Importing a Design
item.description:
Kanvas acts as a powerful bridge, enabling you to import your existing application and infrastructure configurations from a wide variety of standard formats. It transforms these configurations into visual, editable, deployable, and shareable designs. This guide covers how to import designs, the supported formats, and important considerations.

Accessing the Import Functionality 🔗

There are multiple ways to import a design.

You can drag a file from your local computer directly onto the Kanvas canvas to import a design.

item.title: Create Your First Design
item.description:
In this tutorial you build a small web application design in Kanvas Designer: a Deployment that runs the application, a ConfigMap that holds its settings, and a Service that exposes it. You start from an empty canvas, connect the components, and save the result. The saved design is the starting point for Deploy and Observe Your First Design.

Along the way you learn what a design is made of, how relationships express the way components depend on each other, and when and how Kanvas saves your work.

item.title: Deploy and Observe Your First Design
item.description:
In this tutorial you take the design you saved in Create Your First Design to a live Kubernetes cluster. You validate it, dry-run it against the cluster, deploy it, and then switch to Operator mode to see the running resources that belong to the design. You finish by undeploying it.

Along the way you learn the difference between checking a design against its schemas and checking it against a cluster, how Kanvas chooses where to deploy, and how Kanvas keeps track of the resources a design creates.
